subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally persist session defaults, but the reported failure mode can preserve a weaker exec policy after an operator tightens configuration.

options.title: Make config a security ceiling
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp persisted session fields that exceed it, with migration or reset coverage.

options.title: Keep session persistence as documented
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing channel lanes.

options.title: Ship operator reset first
options.body: Add an explicit session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for already-persisted sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config a security ceiling
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp persisted session fields that exceed it, with migration or reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override feature and tests points to this owner candidate.
